subproblem.title: Interior product of a unit orientation with a unit tangent vector (Simon Ch. 6, 4.3)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ and Q ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace. Let ζ be an (n+1)-vector, i.e. a continuous linear functional on (n+1)-covectors of ℝ^P (MultiVector P (n+1)), which is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q). This means: there is an orthonormal τ = (τ₀, …, τₙ) spanning Q with ζ(β) = β(τ) for all β, or ζ(β) = −β(τ) for all β. Let ν ∈ Q with |ν| = 1. Let ζ' be an n-vector (MultiVector P n) with ζ'(α) = ζ(ν♭ ∧ α) for every n-covector α. Here
 ν♭ ∧ α := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ ν).smulRight α),
 that is, (ν♭∧α)(v₀, …, vₙ) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, v_i⟩ α(v₀, …, v̂_i, …, vₙ).
Then ζ' is a unit orientation of Q ∩ ν^⊥ (IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' (Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ζ : MultiVector P (n + 1)) (ζ' : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q → ν ∈ Q → ‖ν‖ = 1 → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ζ' α = ζ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ ν).smulRight α))) → IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' (Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent Step 5 and Step 0(a); Simon Ch. 6, 4.3 (⟨v⌞w, a⟩ = ⟨v, w∧a⟩, and ξ⌞ν is a simple unit n-vector orienting T_xM_t).

1. Dimensions. τ is an orthonormal family of n+1 vectors spanning Q, so dim Q = n+1. Since ν ∈ Q and ν ≠ 0, Q = (ℝ∙ν) ⊕ (Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ) orthogonally (Submodule.sup_orthogonal_inf_of_hasOrthogonalProjection applied to ℝ∙ν ≤ Q, with Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq or the orthogonal direct sum). Hence Q' := Q ∩ ν^⊥ = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ has dimension n. Let σ = (σ₁, …, σₙ) be an orthonormal basis of Q' (e.g. stdOrthonormalBasis of Q', reindexed by Fin n; for n = 0 the empty family). Then ρ := (ν, σ₁, …, σₙ) is an orthonormal family of n+1 vectors in Q, hence an orthonormal basis of Q, and span(range σ) = Q'.

2. Sign lemma (parent Step 0(a)). Write ρ_i = Σ_l m_{il} τ_l. The matrix (m_{il}) is orthogonal, since both families are orthonormal bases of Q, so det(m) = ε₀ ∈ {1, −1} (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Every (n+1)-covector β, restricted to Q (the alternating map β.compLinearMap Q.subtype on Q), is a multiple of the determinant in the basis τ (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). So β(ρ₀, …, ρₙ) = det(m)·β(τ₀, …, τₙ) = ε₀ β(τ). With the sign ε₁ ∈ {1, −1} from IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q, we get ζ(β) = ε₁β(τ) = ε₁ε₀ β(ν, σ₁, …, σₙ) for every β. The sign ε := ε₁ε₀ does not depend on β.

3. Wedge expansion. Let α be an n-covector and put v₀ := ν, v_i := σ_i (i = 1, …, n), i.e. v = Fin.cons ν σ. By the formula for alternatizeUncurryFin (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply: alternatizeUncurryFin F v = Σ_i (−1)^i • F (v i) (Fin.removeNth i v)), by (innerSL ℝ ν)(w) = ⟨ν, w⟩ and by Fin.removeNth 0 (Fin.cons ν σ) = σ:
 (ν♭∧α)(v₀, …, vₙ) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, v_i⟩ α(v without v_i) = ⟨ν, ν⟩ α(σ₁, …, σₙ) + Σ_{i=1}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, σ_i⟩(…) = α(σ₁, …, σₙ),
 since ⟨ν, ν⟩ = 1 and ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ = 0 (σ_i ∈ ν^⊥).

4. Conclusion. For every n-covector α, ζ'(α) = ζ(ν♭∧α) = ε(ν♭∧α)(ν, σ₁, …, σₙ) = ε α(σ). σ is orthonormal with span(range σ) = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ, and either ζ' α = α σ for all α (ε = 1) or ζ' α = −α σ for all α (ε = −1). This is IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' (Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ). ∎
proof_key_steps: dim Q = n+1, so Q ∩ ν^⊥ has an orthonormal basis σ of n vectors and (ν, σ) is an orthonormal basis of Q.
Sign lemma: ζ(β) = ε β(ν, σ) with ε = ±1, the determinant of a change between orthonormal bases.
Wedge expansion: (ν♭∧α)(ν, σ₁, …, σₙ) = α(σ₁, …, σₙ).
Hence ζ'(α) = ε α(σ), i.e. ζ' is a unit orientation of Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ.

audit.reason: The orthogonal decomposition and change-of-basis sign give an adapted orthonormal basis. The verified alternatizeUncurryFin expansion has exactly the stated normalization, so contraction yields a unit orientation, also when n = 0.
